Hi Ravi / Apex procurement team,

Thanks for the time this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a two-sheet model (Apex_GPU_Pricing_Model.xlsx) showing: 1) the deal-level dedicated-capacity sizing that maps to your expected 99th percentile QPS per feature; and 2) three pricing scenarios that reflect potential NVIDIA GPU spot/contract discount moves (base, -10% GPU cost, -20% GPU cost).

Key ask: we need a confirmation from your side on which pricing scenario you want Redwood to base the draft SOW on (base / partial pass-through / full pass-through). Each option changes the monthly committed spend and the unit price that triggers automatic tier migrations in our billing. If you want a hybrid (cap plus pass-through floor), tell us the preferred floor and ceiling.

Practical notes:
- Sizing in sheet "Capacity" assumes a 60ms p95 generation target and a 2x buffer for peak feature rollouts.
- The pricing sheet shows an explicit "GPU cost passthrough" row: if market GPU-hour moves by X, the per-token price will adjust by ~Y after converting usage to GPU-hours.
- If you require a fixed per-token price regardless of GPU-market movement, we can provide a quote with an added risk spread; that requires a minimum 12–18 month commit.

Logistics/next steps: can you confirm which scenario by EOD Thu so we can lock in pricing with finance and legal? I copied Karthik for mutual-action items.

Laura / Evelyn —

Looping you in. Quick read: Ravi wants a cap on monthly passthrough moves and an 18-month pricing view. From finance perspective, the passthrough clause can be implemented as an indexed adjustment (quarterly true-up) or as a fixed uplift for longer tenors. We need to decide which exposes Redwood to GPU spot volatility and what approval band we want for discounts beyond our standard table.

I ran a quick sensitivity (attached: Apex_GPU_Pricing_Model.xlsx tab "Sensitivity") and observed:
- If GPU cost falls 20% and we pass through 50% of the benefit, Redwood's gross margin on this SKU improves by ~6 percentage points.
- If GPU cost rises 15% and passthrough is unlimited, we could see a negative margin tail unless the customer signs up to an 18-month floor.

Proposed internal approach:
1) Offer three contract templates: (A) fixed price (18 months, +5% risk spread), (B) capped-pass-through (cap = +8% monthly adjustment), (C) indexed quarterly true-up with a protective floor.
2) For (B) and (C), any expected discount above 12% requires VP-level approval from Finance.
3) We put a one-time carveout in SOW for a GPU-cost reconciliation report.

Evelyn — can you confirm the approval threshold for discounting beyond tiered pricing? If VP sign-off is required how fast can we get it (we're targeting a week)?

Karthik
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Laura —

Thanks for the summary and sensitivity outputs. Finance guidance below:
- Approval thresholds: discounts or cost-pass-through structures that reduce our forecasted annualized gross margin on this deal by >8 percentage points require VP Finance sign-off. Anything that could lead to negative margin must go to CFO review.
- For indexed passthroughs we prefer a quarterly true-up with a +-10% collar and a floor equal to our 12-month average GPU cost baseline. That collar protects Redwood from rapid spikes.
- An 18-month term with a fixed uplift (our "risk spread") of 4–6% is acceptable and reduces approvals needed.

Operational ask: please attach a version of the pricing model that shows a simple P&L over 24 months (revenue, GPU cost, gross margin) under each scenario. I can pre-approve up to the VP band if the P&L delta is within the 8pp threshold.

Evelyn Hart

Ravi / team,

Thanks for the quick turn. Per internal alignment with Finance (cc'd), Redwood can present the following formal options in the SOW:

Option 1 — Fixed price (18 months): fixed per-token rate; Redwood bears GPU-market variance. Includes a 4.5% risk spread.
Option 2 — Capped pass-through (12 or 18 months): quarterly true-up; monthly adjustment capped at +/-8%; quarterly true-up with a 10% collar and 12-month average floor.
Option 3 — Indexed pass-through (18 months preferred): quarterly indexed true-up, 50% of GPU-cost delta passed to Apex up to a 12% cap; requires VP Finance approval if passthrough share >50% or cap >12%.

I attached an updated one-pager (deal_summary_apex_v1.pdf) and the same pricing model updated with a 24-month P&L tab. Please confirm which option you prefer so we can: 1) draft SOW language; 2) if needed, route for VP approval; 3) schedule a short 30-min call to walk the legal team through the passthrough clause.

If we don't hear back by EOD Thursday we'll assume Option 2 (12-month capped pass-through) and proceed to draft.

Best,
Laura
